headline: The coldest place on Earth, new skills and a holiday house
teaser: Where is the coldest place in the world? What couldn't Leo, Sofia and Kenji do last year? What must the Novak family do at their holiday house?

articles.title: Where Is the Wildest Weather on Earth?
articles.dek: The coldest, the hottest, the wettest, the driest and the windiest: visit five record places.
paras: What is the coldest place on Earth? And where is the hottest? Every country has got its own weather. But some places have the most extreme weather in the world. Scientists measure it and keep records. Let's visit five record places together.

Let's start with the coldest place. It is in Antarctica, near the South Pole. On 21 July 1983, scientists at Vostok Station measured an air temperature of −89.2°C. It is still the lowest temperature in the world's records. A freezer at home is only about −18°C! Nobody can stay outside for long there.

Now let's go to the hottest place. Death Valley is a desert in the USA. On 10 July 1913, the temperature there was 56.7°C. Some scientists think this number is not correct, but it is still the official record. Even today, summer days there are often hotter than 45°C.

For the wettest weather, we have to travel to India. A village called Mawsynram is one of the wettest places on Earth. It gets nearly 12 metres of rain every year. That is as tall as a building with four floors! Most of the rain falls between June and September.

The Atacama Desert in Chile is the opposite. It is the driest desert in the world outside the North and South Poles. Some weather stations there have never recorded any rain at all. The land looks a lot like Mars. That is why scientists test space robots there.

What about wind? The strongest gust of wind ever measured was on Barrow Island in Australia. In April 1996, a big storm hit the island. One gust was 408 kilometres an hour. That is faster than a racing car!

So which place has got the worst weather? It's hard to say! Death Valley isn't as cold as Antarctica, and the Atacama isn't as wet as Mawsynram. Every place is extreme in a different way. Is your town's weather as wild as these places?

grammar.rule: Use the + superlative to say a thing is number one in a group. Short adjectives add -est (cold → the coldest). Long ones use the most (the most extreme). Use as … as for things that are the same, and not as … as for less.

articles.title: Last Year I Couldn't Do It
articles.dek: Three teenagers tell us about something new they can do this year.
paras: Do you remember something you couldn't do a year ago? Maybe you can do it now. Learning something new is not always easy. Sometimes you feel scared or silly. We asked three teenagers about a new skill.

Hi, I'm Leo, and I'm thirteen. Last summer, I couldn't swim. All my friends could swim, so I felt embarrassed at the beach. I always stayed on the sand with my little sister. In September, I started lessons at the sports centre. At first, I swallowed a lot of water! But my teacher was very kind. Now I can swim fifty metres without stopping. I still can't dive, but I'm going to learn next year.

My name is Sofia, and I'm fifteen. A year ago, I was very shy. I couldn't speak in front of my class. My face went red, and I forgot all my words. Then my English teacher asked me to join the school drama club. I didn't want to go, but I went. We played funny games and acted in short plays. Slowly, I became brave. Last month I gave a talk to two hundred students, and I wasn't nervous at all!

I'm Kenji, and I'm fourteen. My grandma lives with us, and she cooks every day. Last year I couldn't cook anything, not even an egg. Then Grandma broke her arm, and she couldn't use the kitchen for six weeks. So she sat on a chair and gave me instructions. I burned the rice two times! But now I can make soup, noodles and her famous dumplings. Grandma says mine are almost as good as hers.
What can you do now? What couldn't you do last year? Write and tell us about it. We'd love to hear your story!

articles.title: Notes at the Holiday House
articles.dek: Where is the key? What goes in the green bin? Read the notes and find out.
paras: The Novak family is spending a week at a holiday house by the sea. When they arrived, they found lots of notes from the owner, Mrs Brown. The family also wrote some messages. Here are some of them.

NOTE on the front door: Welcome! The key for the back door is under the blue plant pot. You don't have to lock the back door during the day, but you must lock both doors at night. Please put the keys back in the box when you leave.

SIGN in the kitchen: Please read! You have to wash and dry your plates before you go. You don't have to clean the oven – my cleaner does that. Don't put food in the small bin. Food waste must go in the green bin outside.

NOTE on the washing machine: This machine is very old! You must close the door hard, or it won't start. Wait five minutes before you open it. Beach towels are in the cupboard by the stairs, so you don't have to bring your own.

Text message from Mum to Petra: Hi Petra, Dad and I are at the supermarket. Can you take Max for a walk? Remember, he has to stay on his lead near the road. And he mustn't eat Mrs Brown's flowers again! We'll be back at twelve.
Note on the fridge from Dad: Kids, we have to leave at nine tomorrow morning, so please pack your bags tonight. You don't have to make breakfast. I'm going to buy croissants at the café. Dad

Message in the visitors' book from Petra: We loved this house! The beds were very comfortable, and the view of the sea was amazing. My brother didn't want to go home. Next time we must stay for two weeks! Thank you, Mrs Brown. Petra Novak (14)

grammar.point: must / have to / don't have to
grammar.rule: must and have to + verb mean it is necessary. don't have to means it isn't necessary, but you can if you want. mustn't means don't do it! For the past, use had to.
table: He has to stay on his lead.
You don't have to clean the oven.

examples.text: You don't have to lock the back door during the day, but you must lock both doors at night.
You have to wash and dry your plates before you go.
You don't have to clean the oven – my cleaner does that.
And he mustn't eat Mrs Brown's flowers again!

kps.fact: You must close the old washing machine door hard.
kps.q: What happens if you don't close the door hard?

kps.fact: Max the dog has to stay on his lead near the road.
kps.q: Where does Max have to stay on his lead?

mindmap.question: What do the notes and messages tell the Novak family?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the texts.
summary.model: Mrs Brown left notes because the family had to follow some house rules. The Novaks loved the house, so they want to come back.

options.t: The owner left notes with rules for the house.
options.why: Most texts are Mrs Brown's notes.
options.evidence: When they arrived, they found lots of notes from the owner, Mrs Brown.

options.t: The family wrote messages about the dog and leaving.
options.why: Mum and Dad wrote messages too.
options.evidence: Kids, we have to leave at nine tomorrow morning, so please pack your bags tonight.

options.t: Petra loved the house and wants to stay longer next time.
options.why: This is how the holiday ends.
options.evidence: Next time we must stay for two weeks!

options.t: The beach towels are in the cupboard by the stairs.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: Beach towels are in the cupboard by the stairs, so you don't have to bring your own.

options.t: Mrs Brown lives next door to the holiday house.
The family must clean the oven before they leave.
options.why: Wrong: they don't have to clean the oven.
options.evidence: You don't have to clean the oven – my cleaner does that.

speak.p: What jobs do you have to do at home? Which jobs don't you have to do?
speak.hint: I have to … every day. / I don't have to … because …

write.p: You are staying at a friend's house. Write a note to your friend's mum. Write 25 words or more.
steps: Ask if you have to do a job (wash plates, make your bed…).
Say what time you must go home.
